## Dreamstep (A lullaby for the grave)

The largest omission that fans will call out is my hit DJ mix "A lullaby for the grave." I've been lucid dreaming since 2001. To say that the movie _Inception_ hit me in a personal way is to make a grievous understatement. I immediately started sampling the movie, pulling out quotes, as well as samples from other movies to weave together a set based on dreams in the genres of trap, dubstep, future garage, and transnational beats (among others). Fans of "[The ADHD Revolution](adhd-revolution)" heard some early versions. Less than a year after _Inception_ came out, I was ready to release the first version of the set to the public.

The response was... _not small._

I've played versions of it live at Burning Man, at Love Fest in Florida, and of course a few underground parties. It hasn't been requested in years, but I still keep it up and play it whenever the mood hits.

So for those dreamers out there (nightmares included), _this one's for you!_

\[[Stream on Mixcloud](https://www.mixcloud.com/JayaPrime/dreamstep-a-lullaby-for-the-grave/)\]

## CD2: Tears of Ra

**DJ Jaya Prime**, _A Study in Forces_

In thanks to Tristan Skybreak, Marf, Gaea Phoenix, and DJ Ezra B Rich spreading this CD around (amongst others), it's literally how I became known as "Jaya" outside of just the Hare Krishna enclaves that I spent part of my time as a monk with. The name spread ahead of me... it stuck! To this day, almost everyone calls me Jaya. This mix focused on 4x4s with trance and house at the forefront. The full version isn't online, but the "cream of the crop" cut from the middle of the mix has been saved for you to stream. True to form, over the years this original album has been eclipsed by _"[Blood of the Moon](blood-of-the-moon)"_ (and, to some extent, CD3). This is my very first DJ mix, released between late 2001 and summer of 2002 when I burned it to CDs. You can see Gaea's copy of the CD here below.

\[[Stream on Mixcloud](https://www.mixcloud.com/JayaPrime/adhf-houseparty-set-oldskool-acid-house/)\]

## CD3: Twilight

**DJ Jaya Prime**, _A Study in Forces_

The final album in the series came out late in 2004, basically kicking off 2005, which put it in the unfortunate position to compete against the resurgence of [The Happy Fun Pak + The adHF](adhd-revolution), the rise of [Trochlear Recordings](trochlear-recordings), my first live DJ shows _and_ my first live shows as a band, PLUS my very first pilgrimage to Black Rock City, Nevada for _"Burning Man: The Psyche"_ (WOWWWWW!!!!), and even getting together with DJ Ezra B Rich to put down an official remix of "Turn Off the Lights" by Nelly Furtado. Oh yeah, and all while rocking it out with DC at Thundercloud, including our crazy jam-packed in-store party for St Patty's Day that year. Even had _Twilight_ been given a fighting shot, most were asking me to mix my _"[Blood of the Moon](blood-of-the-moon)"_ set whenever they had the chance. It wasn't forgotten though. Crowd favorites like the closing three songs were later worked into the greater MP3CD version of "Blood of the Moon", which you can download here below:

[DOWNLOAD:99-GoodnightSweetTerra.mp3]

Then I've set aside some of my own favorites from the original mix here:

\[[Selections on Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/489C9HDmPIvpxdPssIqSYC?si=e501c31f4d1f4677)\]

texts:
##### For what remains...

##### For those who remember...

This list is by no means comprehensive. Not by a long-shot, Love... not at all. With DJ sets, I always customize them to the audience, like playing Sarah Slean's cover of "Climbing Up the Walls" ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w2tWWBwzhbY)) for Namen's birthday party or "[Teardrop on Roads](teardrop-on-roads)" at Burning Man for Disco Lama. Most have been lost along the way. Others that should've been forgotten have remained, such as my just-playing-around mix for a chillout houseparty that you can still find [here on Mixcloud](https://www.mixcloud.com/JayaPrime/4am-atx-take-2-1-hour-triphop-downtempo-mixtape/)... or my dubstep DJ set for The BuzzInn at Burning Man. In fact, that one's also [up on Mixcloud](https://www.mixcloud.com/JayaPrime/smoke-dust-and-ashes/). They each have their fans, so I don't delete them, but neither do I identify with them. I've mixed and remixed "[The ADHD Revolution](adhd-revolution)" what must be a thousand different ways depending on the party. So if you don't see one of your favs listed here, it was probably lost along the way. But! If you do remember one that isn't listed, and you can give me context from when and where I played it, then maybe it can be recreated. [Send me a line](contact) and I'll take a look. Because from what remains... and for those who remember. .. those are the moments that matter.

_<font face="Courier New">Every second of them.</font>_
"They Held Each Other And Kissed   And Pushed Each Others'   Darkness into the Corner, Believing in each others' Light,         each others' Dream"
\- Hubert Selby, Jr. (July 23, 1928 – April 26, 2004), Requiem for a Dream
